items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Harry Garnett, he was one that played, I found out later, why Alexander liked the band so

ctx.x: And so he told me, he said, I'll tell you what, I don't think any of your arrangements arrange as hard as me, but Amos finally gets it and when he gets it he's got it, you know, and I think you shouldn't worry about that. I was talking to Harry Garnett, there wasn't anybody there in Tulsa that I knew that I could get, or in the area, and Harry Garnett, he was one that played, I found out later, why Alexander liked the band so, he was on the style of Herschel Evans, at that time,

and Bud Douglas, another tenor man was something like Pres, and so they just knocked him out. So anyway, he said I know a man in Chicago I can get, play anything you have in your book--that's Harry Garnett--but I don't know if he would fit like Amos; Amos sure fit this band good. And I finally decided I better give him his notice while I got time. So I gave Amos the notice and of course he was going around like he lost his mother or something; all the rest of the band just grinning and this young man came in and…
